bio:
Thomas Topping was baptized as 'Thomas Toppyn' at Totternhoe in Bedfordshire, England, on 19 March 1608/9, the son of John Topping. He married Emma Aldridge at Dunstable on 16 November 1628, and their eldest son Thomas was baptized at Totternhoe on 25 October 1629. By 1636 he was at Wraysbury in Buckinghamshire, the parish that contains Magna Carta Island, where on 12 April of that year he was one of two overseers who reported to the manor court that 'all was well with the water courses'.

He was in New England by 1639, when he was Wethersfield's deputy to the Connecticut General Court. He moved to Milford in 1639 or 1640, joined the Milford church with his wife Emma in 1640, and had two sons baptized there, Elnathan on 2 August 1640 and James on 12 February 1643. He then settled at Southampton on Long Island, where he was 'many years a magistrate'. 'Topping's Purchase' was secured by Indian deeds of 1662 and 1666, paid for with twenty fathoms of wampum. In 1662 he was named in King Charles II's charter for Connecticut, 'one of the company to whom King Charles granted his letters patent for the Colony of Connecticut'.

He married three times. After Emma's death he made a marriage contract on 20 October 1666 with Mary, widow of Timothy Baldwin, and by June 1678 his third wife was Lydia, widow of John Wilford. On 5 October 1686, at Branford, he deeded his Southampton lands to his sons Elnathan and James. He died at Branford, Connecticut, in December 1687. The old account that he fled England as a 'refugee from religious persecution' is family tradition only. His service as captain, magistrate and deputy is of the kind that qualifies descendants for the Society of Colonial Wars, though John's descent through Temperance Smith depends on her parentage, which is not yet settled. He was John's 11th-great-grandfather.

researchNotes:
Baptized 'Thomas Toppyn' at Totternhoe, Bedfordshire, 19 Mar 1608/9, son of John. Married Emma Aldridge at Dunstable 16 Nov 1628; eldest son Thomas baptized at Totternhoe 25 Oct 1629. A Wraysbury, Bucks., court roll of 12 Apr 1636 names him one of two overseers reporting that 'all was well with the water courses' (Wraysbury parish contains Magna Carta Island). At Wethersfield, Conn., by 1639 and its deputy to the CT General Court in 1639; Milford 1639/40; then Southampton. 'Topping's Purchase': Indian deeds of 1662 and 1666, paid with 20 fathoms of wampum. Named in King Charles II's 1662 charter for Connecticut — Savage: 'one of the company to whom King Charles granted his letters patent for the Colony of Connecticut' (Conn. Hist. Soc. Coll. 3:306). Married three times. In 1686 deeded his Southampton lands to sons Elnathan and James. Died at Branford, Dec 1687 (1687/8), 'many years a magistrate'. Howell's 1887 'refugee from religious persecution' is family tradition only. Society of Colonial Wars: captain, magistrate, deputy — qualifying, but route depends on Temperance's parentage. Round 1 moved him from 10th to 11th great-grandfather (13 generations). TREE: 'Captain T I Topping 1608–1687 + Emma C Aldridge… 1610–1665 (ship image)', shown as father of John Topping (1636–1686) — that line (John → Josiah → Jerusha) is removed.

Savage (vol. 4, p. 255) records that Thomas Topping of Milford joined the Milford church 'with his w. Emma in 1640' and 'had Elnathan, bapt. 2 Aug. of that yr. and James, 12 Feb. 1643' ([R4-S1]). That fixes Capt. Elnathan's baptism, 2 Aug 1640. Savage also notes the 20 Oct 1666 marriage contract with Mary, widow of Timothy Baldwin, the third wife Lydia (widow of John Wilford) by June 1678, and the 5 Oct 1686 Branford deed of his Southampton lands to sons Elnathan and James ([R4-S1], [R4-S2]).
